audit_findings.title: Known tariff reversal may make the FY2025 earnings anchor stale
audit_findings.mechanism: Could reduce future customs-brokerage owner earnings and invalidate the assumed 0%-6% growth from the FY2025 anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The ruling invalidates many of the tariffs imposed on imports to the United States in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated anchor error. Results after the February 2026 ruling show customs-brokerage and other-services revenue up 22% and operating income up 25% for the first half of 2026, while management attributed continued demand to customs complexity. New tariffs were also imposed in July 2026. The feared earnings reversal was therefore not present in the latest filed numbers, although future simplification or lower trade volumes could still reduce earnings.
audit_findings.action: Monitor quarterly customs-clearance volumes, declaration fees, post-entry work, related staffing and segment profitability; rerun the anchor or growth cases if those measures show a sustained post-tariff decline.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may include operating cash rather than distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $1,031.448 million, equal to $7.85 per share and 8.6% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any required operating cash should be removed from the cash bridge to avoid adding cash while also capitalizing the earnings it supports.
audit_findings.evidence: As a customs broker, we make significant short-term cash advances for a select group of our credit-worthy customers.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributable portion remains unresolved, but even the extreme correction of removing the entire $1.031 billion cash balance would reduce base value from $90.98 to about $83.13 per share. It would not change the conclusion relative to the $188.80 market price, and the actual correction must be smaller because the company plainly holds some excess or investable cash.
audit_findings.action: Calculate minimum operating cash after customer advances, seasonal working capital, foreign liquidity requirements and repatriation costs; rerun the bridge only with cash above that requirement.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified Indian tax disputes could create a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse settlement would reduce the equity bridge through a cash claim or reduce owner earnings through additional tax, interest and penalties.
audit_findings.evidence: However, if these matters are adversely resolved, we would recognize significant additional tax expense, including interest and penalties.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved contingent claim, not a demonstrated valuation error. The June 2026 filing reports that India's Supreme Court dismissed a significant portion of the claims, but remaining matters could still produce significant expense. The company cannot estimate the loss range and says recorded contingencies are not significant, so the record cannot establish whether the residual exposure is material to value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the asserted amounts and issues remaining after the Supreme Court ruling, applicable reserves, interest and penalty calculations, limitation periods and counsel's probability assessment; deduct the probability-weighted claim and rerun if it becomes estimable.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital expenditure may be understated by the FY2025 run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.899 million annual difference; approximately $0.75 per base-case share if entirely recurring
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher recurring maintenance capital expenditure would reduce annual owner earnings and therefore operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Total anticipated capital expenditures in 2026 are currently estimated to be approximately $100 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The original $100 million plan was superseded by the June 2026 filing's approximately $60 million estimate, while first-half expenditure was $24.603 million. Even treating the entire $6.899 million increase over FY2025's $53.101 million as recurring maintenance would reduce the $777.4 million anchor by only 0.9% and base value by approximately $0.75 per share. That scale cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Separate the revised $60 million plan into maintenance and growth expenditure; rerun only if normalized recurring maintenance materially exceeds $60 million or the FY2025 deduction.

audit_findings.title: An active ESPP offering may be absent from the valuation-date share ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.893 million withheld; resulting share dilution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Shares issued under the July 31, 2026 ESPP purchase would increase the fully diluted denominator and reduce per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: A total of 15,884 shares have been issued under the 2002 Plan since inception and $ 28,893 has been withheld from employees at December 31, 2025 in connection with the plan year ending July 31, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes funded purchase rights and states that ESPP shares are issued in the third quarter, but it does not state the July 31 issuance quantity in the supplied record. The valuation ceiling exceeds the July 31 outstanding count of 129.990622 million by 1.405 million shares, which may already be sufficient, but the record does not demonstrate that the allowance includes the completed offering. Materiality therefore cannot be conclusively established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the exact July 31, 2026 ESPP shares issued and reconcile them, together with RSUs, PSUs and other dilutive awards, to the 131.395622 million ceiling; rerun per-share values if the reconciled ceiling is higher.

audit_findings.title: The anchor retains an unusually adverse foreign-exchange result
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 loss $28.233 million; three-year average loss $10.540 million; implied pretax normalization $17.693 million, approximately $1.89 per base-case share before tax
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalizing an unusually large transactional loss would increase anchor owner earnings and operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Net foreign currency transactional losses were approximately $28 million in 2025, and net foreign currency transactional gains were approximately $12 million in 2024, net of taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed history shows recurring two-way currency exposure: a $14.943 million loss in 2023, an $11.556 million gain in 2024 and a $28.233 million loss in 2025. Normalizing FY2025 to the three-year average would add $17.693 million before tax and approximately $1.89 per share to base value before tax effects. Even adding back the entire FY2025 loss would increase base value by only about $3.02 per share before tax, insufficient to change the conclusion relative to $188.80.
audit_findings.action: Compile the full ten-year transactional-gain-and-loss series and identify exceptional exposures; rerun with a long-run normalized amount only if the FY2025 loss is demonstrably nonrecurring.
